Welcome to
The Railway Hotel Fordingbridge
The Railway Hotel Fordingbridge is a characterful boutique hotel, pub and restaurant, perfectly placed for exploring the New Forest and the surrounding Hampshire countryside.
Stay in one of our five en-suite rooms or our charming self-contained two-bedroom cottage, then relax with a drink in the bar or enjoy lunch or dinner in our distinctive Pullman dining carriage.
Whether you are joining us for a meal, a drink or a few days away, we look forward to welcoming you to The Railway Hotel.
We accept cash and all major debit/credit card payments.

Dining at the Railway Hotel
Step aboard our First Class Pullman dining carriage and enjoy freshly prepared food in one of Fordingbridge’s most distinctive places to eat. Our menus bring together pub favourites, seasonal dishes and regularly changing specials, with plenty of choice whether you are joining us for lunch, dinner or something relaxed with a drink.
Choose a cosy booth in the Pullman carriage, dine in the bar or take a table in our light and spacious Observation Carriage , which opens directly onto the courtyard. When the weather is on our side, you can also eat outside in the courtyard or on Platform 2 , the perfect spot for a leisurely lunch, an evening meal or pizza and drinks in the sunshine.
Families are very welcome, with options for younger diners alongside vegetarian and other dietary choices. If you have a particular allergy or dietary requirement, please speak to a member of the team, and we will be happy to advise.
View Menus
Fordingbridge is easily accessible from Salisbury in the north, and Bournemouth in the south on the A338. From the M27 continue west on to the A31 before joining the A338 at Ringwood. We have free on-site parking for when you get here.

About The Railway Hotel Fordingbridge | Pub, Dining & Rooms
Skip to content
Hotel · Pub · Dining · Fordingbridge
The Railway Hotel, Fordingbridge
A historic Victorian hotel, pub and dining destination in Fordingbridge, Hampshire,
welcoming locals and visitors for food, drink and distinctive boutique accommodation.
The Railway Hotel has been a Fordingbridge landmark for more than 160 years. Built
in the 1860s by Dorchester brewer Eldridge Pope, the hotel originally served passengers
travelling through the nearby Fordingbridge Railway Station on the Salisbury and Dorset Railway line.
Following a major refurbishment that carefully restored the Victorian building and
celebrated its railway heritage, The Railway Hotel reopened under new management on
5 August 2026.
Stay With Us
Food & Drink
More than 160 years of history
A Fordingbridge hotel built for the railway age
The history of The Railway Hotel is closely connected with the arrival of the railway
in Fordingbridge and the Victorian expansion of the town.
The Railway Hotel was built in the 1860s by Dorchester brewer
Eldridge Pope and originally served passengers using
Fordingbridge Railway Station.
The station stood on the Salisbury and Dorset Railway line, making the hotel
part of the experience of arriving in and departing from Fordingbridge during
the golden age of railway travel.
That history remains central to the character of the hotel today. Its restoration,
bedrooms and dining spaces have all been designed to retain the Victorian character
of the building while celebrating its connection with classic railway travel.
1860s
The hotel is built
Dorchester brewer Eldridge Pope builds The Railway Hotel to serve passengers
using Fordingbridge Railway Station.
Railway Era
Serving Fordingbridge
The hotel becomes part of the town's railway story beside the Salisbury and
Dorset Railway line.
Restoration
Victorian character restored
A major refurbishment lasting around two years restores the building with careful
attention to its heritage.
2026
A new chapter
The Railway Hotel reopens under new management on 5 August 2026.
Reopened August 2026
A new chapter for The Railway Hotel
The Railway Hotel officially reopened on 5 August 2026 under new publican
Jason Schinkel .
Jason brings extensive hospitality experience to The Railway Hotel following his
tenure at The Three Lions and, previously, the Horse and Groom in Woodgreen.
The initial focus is firmly on the pub and dining, serving a selection of meals and
lighter bites, while the hotel's distinctive accommodation is also available for
visitors looking for somewhere to stay in the Fordingbridge area.
The reopening brings one of Fordingbridge's longstanding hospitality landmarks back
into use for local residents, diners and visitors to the area.

Boutique hotel rooms
Inspired by iconic railway journeys
The refurbishment introduced five individually designed en-suite guest rooms,
each celebrating the glamour and romance of classic railway travel.
Rooms are named after iconic trains including the Orient Express ,
Bournemouth Belle and Flying Scotsman , with interiors
designed around the character and romance of the railway age.
The Railway Hotel also has a self-contained two-bedroom cottage and accessible guest
facilities, providing additional options for visitors looking for accommodation in
the Fordingbridge area.
Discover Our Rooms
Carefully restored
Victorian character brought back to life
The reopening followed a major refurbishment by Larasian that took around two years
to complete.
Particular attention was given to preserving and celebrating the heritage of this
Victorian Fordingbridge building while creating a hotel, pub and dining destination
for today.
The railway story now continues throughout the property, from the individually
designed bedrooms to dining areas inspired by the golden age of rail travel.
Fordingbridge · Hampshire
Stay, eat and drink in Fordingbridge
The Railway Hotel is located on Station Road in Fordingbridge, Hampshire, welcoming
local residents as well as visitors staying in and exploring the surrounding area.
With pub, dining and accommodation together in one historic property, The Railway
Hotel provides a convenient place to meet, eat or stay while visiting Fordingbridge.
Our five en-suite bedrooms and two-bedroom cottage also make the hotel a useful base
for guests looking for accommodation in the Fordingbridge area and those travelling
on to explore the wider New Forest and Hampshire countryside.

Room 01 · 24 m²
The Orient Express
DELUXE KING-SIZE ROOM
Bold colours, rich fabrics and Eastern-inspired furnishings give the Orient Express its distinctive character. A four-poster king-size bed and spacious en-suite bathroom make this a particularly comfortable place to unwind.
Four-poster king-size bed

History behind the name
Developed by Georges Nagelmackers, the Orient Express made its inaugural journey from Paris on 4 October 1883. Over the years its routes changed, but its name became closely associated with luxurious journeys across Europe.
